_readme: EXTERNAL MCP SERVERS the served model can call. Read by harness/mcp_server/bridge.py.
WHAT DOES NOT BELONG HERE: this repo's OWN server (`python -m harness.mcp_server`).
It was the only entry until 2026-07-31 and it was a LOOP — it exposes the same
harness skills she already has natively, so 9 of its 10 tools were shadowed and
skipped, and the net gain was `disk_free`, an EXAMPLE function in a file whose
docstring literally says 'Example:'. Two and a quarter seconds per call to reach a
five-line helper she could already have written in run_python.
harness/mcp_server IS STILL WORTH HAVING — it just points the other way. It is the
OUTBOUND surface: how Claude Code, LM Studio, or any MCP client reaches HER memory
and skills. See MCP-README.md. The gate fixture that still needs a self-connection
tool whose name a native tool owns is NAMESPACED to <server>_<name>, never dropped.

_why: A REAL browser, which is the one thing her web tools could not do. web_search
and web_fetch READ a page; this one can open it, click, fill a form, and see
what came back. --headless --isolated means it needs no pre-running Chrome and
TELEMETRY OFF, DELIBERATELY. chrome-devtools-mcp sends usage statistics to
Google, and trace URLs to the CrUX API, BY DEFAULT. This is his machine and her
browsing; neither flag is a preference.
`allow` keeps 7 of its 29 tools. The rest are lighthouse audits, performance
traces and heap snapshots — real tools, just not ones she has any use for, and
every entry in the load-on-demand index costs prompt budget whether she ever
take_screenshot collides with her native sight tool, so it arrives as
browser_take_screenshot. Native keeps the bare name.
